name: Silvio Berlusconi
role: Italian media entrepreneur and Prime Minister of Italy (1994-95, 2001-06, 2008-11)
summary: Silvio Berlusconi, founder of Forza Italia and four-time Italian Prime Minister, governed as a liberal-conservative centre-right leader: tax cuts, nuclear power, tougher immigration control and an alliance with the Catholic Church on life issues, with repeated attacks on prosecutors and wiretaps.

notes: First audit, from his Prime Minister's speeches and interviews of 2008-2011 in the EUSpeech corpus (machine translation of the Italian originals, so medium at most) read by theme: the May 2008 programme speeches, interviews on taxes, immigration and Libya, euthanasia and the Englaro decree, wiretaps and immunity, the Church, Israel and the Palestinians. These are in-office statements of a head of government and are his words, but each speaks for his government; none is above medium. Searched without a settled answer: Putin and Russia (he mediated between Russia and the US on the missile dispute; no position on arming insurgents or alliances), Iraq and Afghanistan (troop contingents mentioned, no position), privatisation (accepts proposals for it), judicial reform (he wants separation of careers of prosecutors and judges; no matching statement), strong leaders, press ownership. ParlaMint's two 2013 utterances state no position. The Lodo Alfano (Law 124/2008, text on Wikisource, and the Constitutional Court judgment of 2009) is the one act cited, for sovereign-above-law. The El Mundo interview of March 2009 defending immunity was read and is not cited (it would mix words with the act). The Englaro emergency decree and the Libya treaty texts were not reached (see notFound), so those answers rest on his words. Many statements are modern or ideological and stay null.
